review_kind: Assigned owner written mathematical audit; not the HMZ reviewer verdict and not full Lean checking
owner_conclusion: No mathematical error found in the written counterexample after checking the exact finite criterion, stage exponents, every-prefix argument and pooled subsequence. Parent independent audit was requested. The strict HMZ acceptance gate is not met.
checked_steps: rho has the fixed curvature bounds 3/4 and 5/4. Its even-integer support contrast is rho(e-t)-rho(e)=rho(t)-e*t. Both are also formalized in Formal.lean.

N_j=N_(j-1)^10; the fixed law has a largest atom at zero, distinct translates are identifiable, and both first absolute moment and variance are infinite. The law therefore does not contradict Theorem 9's finite-variance hypothesis.

Previous strong coefficient sum is O(N_j^(6/5)), previous weak coefficient sum O(N_j^(3/40)), previous weak second moment V_(j-1)=O(N_j^(3/10)). Buffer weak score ratios have exponents -9/40 and -1/20.

The probabilities of an oversized error in the previous-plus-buffer rows, new strong block, and new low block are respectively O(N_j^(-9/10)), O(N_j^(-9)), and O(N_j^(-1/4)). They vanish without conditioning the truncated variance calculation on the good event.

For each deterministic low-block prefix, the independent truncated weak score has variance V_(j-1)*w, and w/(B_j^2+w)^2 <= 1/(4 B_j^2). This proves a probability bound uniform over prefix choices, not an unproved almost-sure maximum over all prefixes.

The transformed strong coordinate u and weak coordinate v are first proved jointly tight using the two equations; u-K_j=o_P(1) is deduced only afterward. Integer cancellation then makes the weak derivative at zero, divided by its weak Gram weight, o_P(1), giving v=o_P(1).

The buffer and partial-high-block bounds separately control intermediate prefixes. Old rows are retained, no design coefficient is changed after insertion, and all stages contain finite integer counts.
The pooled high-score event has exact probability (1/2)*(1-1/N_j)^(2*N_j-1), tending to exp(-2)/2. Removing all bad-score/tail events costs o(1) unconditionally.
On that event the pooled u approaches 1/2, the cycle weak derivative divided by C_j approaches 4*eta, and Q_j/C_j approaches 8. The global upper curvature bounds the root away from zero by eta/(9M).
